title: Revealed: More than 1,000 NHS operations cancelled due to record UK heatwaves - Carbon Brief
gist: An FOI investigation of 140 NHS trusts found 1,110 operations cancelled due to heat across just 17 days of the UK's May and June 2026 heatwaves, including 10 emergency surgeries and 18 abandoned mid-procedure, with the failure mode being operating-theatre ventilation systems that stop working above a threshold temperature. Because most trusts do not record heat as a cancellation reason at all, the number is a significant undercount of a physical-infrastructure adaptation gap that the government is addressing with only £32m from a £1.5bn programme.

insights.claim: An FOI investigation of 140 NHS trusts and health boards in England and Wales found 1,110 heat-related surgery cancellations across a 17-day window covering 22-28 May and 18-27 June 2026.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: First quantified measure of heat disruption to UK surgical throughput — a template metric other health systems will be asked for.
insights.locator: In total, 59 trusts and health boards responded

insights.claim: Only 59 of 140 NHS trusts provided details of heat-related cancellations, 63 responded without such detail — most saying they simply do not record it — and 19 did not respond at all, making the 1,110 figure a significant underestimate.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The measurement system itself is the gap: climate-impact exposure in public health is materially unmeasured, so headline damage figures should be treated as floors.
insights.locator: Less than half of the NHS trusts provided details

insights.claim: At least 10 emergency operations for life-threatening conditions were cancelled because of heat and another 18 surgeries had to be abandoned midway through.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Heat is already crossing from inconvenience into acute clinical risk, which raises the political salience of hospital cooling capex.
insights.locator: There were also 10 “emergency” operations cancelled

insights.claim: Among trusts that supplied full cancellation datasets, around 7% of all surgery cancellations in the heatwave period were heat-related.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A quantified share that lets analysts scale heat disruption against existing NHS backlog drivers such as staffing and bed shortages.
insights.locator: Of the trusts that provided full datasets

insights.claim: Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust reported the most cancellations at 140, all in the surgery unit at Crawley Hospital, where June temperatures approached 36C.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
entities: Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust
insights.so_what: Damage concentrates in single non-resilient buildings, so remediation spend is targetable rather than system-wide.
insights.locator: Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust reported the most cancellations

insights.claim: Cancellation hotspots — Surrey and Sussex, south Essex, Dudley in the West Midlands, south Wales and parts of London — cluster in the regions that recorded the highest temperatures.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Geographic correlation with peak temperature means future heat maps can forecast disruption locations.
insights.locator: Other hotspots for cancellations include south Essex

insights.claim: Of 596 cancellations for which procedure detail was given, 167 were orthopaedic surgeries such as knee and hip replacements, with eye, gynaecological and urological surgeries also frequently cancelled, plus at least eight heart operations and seven skin-cancer removals.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Identifies which procedure lines — and therefore which device and implant suppliers — see volume pushed out during heat events.
insights.locator: Each dot in the graphic below indicates a cancelled surgery

themes.theme: Ventilation as the physical failure point

insights.claim: The main reason operations stop in heat is that the complex ventilation systems in operating theatres — which dilute airborne contaminants, remove anaesthetic fumes and direct airflow away from the patient — can fail above a certain temperature, according to NHS anaesthetist Ed Robinson.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The bottleneck is a specific engineering subsystem, making theatre HVAC retrofit the direct investable fix rather than generic 'resilience' spending.
insights.quote: We have generalised airflow systems that make the air in theatre flow outwards to adjacent areas, so pathogens and fumes get carried away from the patient into non-clinical areas. When it gets to a certain heat, those systems can fail.
insights.locator: ‘Increased risks’

insights.claim: In 48 recorded cases staff specified the cancellation was due to air conditioning or ventilation units that were broken or unable to sustain appropriate temperatures, rather than a generic statement that it was too hot.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Explicit equipment-failure attribution strengthens the procurement case for cooling and ventilation upgrades.
insights.locator: Although most hospitals simply stated that it was “too hot”

insights.claim: Excess humidity in operating theatres can condense on surgical implements and transmit infections, according to Royal College of Surgeons of England president Tim Lane.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
entities: Royal College of Surgeons of England
insights.so_what: Humidity, not just temperature, is the binding constraint — relevant to what specification any cooling retrofit must meet.
insights.locator: If air in operating theatres is too humid

insights.claim: Heat degrades staff performance because surgical teams wear PPE and, in orthopaedics, heavy lead aprons they cannot remove between X-rays, so a failed ventilation system makes it unsafe to even start an operation.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Explains why orthopaedics is the most-cancelled specialty and why cooling cannot be solved by patient-side measures alone.
insights.quote: So if the ventilation system is not working, you’re going to overheat [and] that’s going to affect your ability to concentrate and perform a safe operation. You just wouldn’t start under those conditions.
insights.locator: Staff are usually wearing PPE

insights.claim: Certain medications and pieces of equipment are not validated for use outside specific temperature ranges, including the cement used to secure hip and knee replacements, which can set too quickly at higher temperatures.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A regulatory/validation constraint on medical consumables that heat exposes — a product-specification risk for device makers.
insights.locator: There are also “certain pieces of equipment and medications”

insights.claim: A study after the record heat of 2022 concluded UK surgical services were poorly prepared for heatwaves, with staff surveys indicating ambient temperatures could not be controlled in two-fifths of NHS operating theatres.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A 40% uncontrolled-theatre rate sizes the addressable retrofit market and shows the problem was documented four years before it materialised at scale.
insights.locator: ‘Poorly prepared’

insights.claim: Every few days of heatwave cancellations lengthens waiting lists and patients' conditions can deteriorate for every week they wait, according to NHS Wales national clinical director Richard Egan.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Heat disruption compounds into the politically sensitive waiting-list metric, raising the odds of emergency funding responses.
insights.quote: That’s a significant impact on waiting lists…For every week that patients are waiting on a waiting list, their condition could get worse and deteriorate.
insights.locator: Richard Egan, an endocrine surgeon

insights.claim: The heat problem is multifactorial — spanning increased patient numbers and staff shortages caused by knock-on effects like heat-related train cancellations — so there is no single solution, according to University of Birmingham surgery researcher Dmitri Nepogodiev.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Climate disruption cascades across infrastructure sectors; rail heat resilience and hospital resilience are linked exposures.
insights.quote: There isn’t a single magic solution because it’s a kind of complex, multifactorial challenge – so it also underlines the importance of broader preparedness.
insights.locator: Nepogodiev notes that the problem of extreme heat extends

insights.claim: The response to extreme heat in surgical theatres has so far been ad hoc, and it may be possible to continue with less risky operations even at higher humidity levels.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Protocol reform is a low-capex mitigation lever that could recover throughput before any hardware is installed.
insights.locator: Egan, who is investigating ways to prepare surgical theatres

insights.claim: Record UK heatwaves in 2026, amplified by climate change, have already been linked to thousands of deaths while the NHS faces record A&E demand, wards reaching unsafe temperatures and equipment failing from heat.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Establishes heat as a recurring systemic stressor on UK health capacity, not a one-off event.
insights.locator: Overheating operations

insights.claim: After this summer's extreme heat the UK government announced £32m from a £1.5bn spending programme for projects strengthening hospitals' resilience to extreme heat, including improved cooling and ventilation systems.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: £32m is roughly 2% of the parent programme against a problem affecting two-fifths of theatres — a visible funding shortfall and a candidate for future top-ups.
insights.locator: Following the extreme heat this summer, the government has announced

insights.claim: The Climate Change Committee has recommended that all UK healthcare buildings should work to maintain safe and appropriate temperatures by 2035, while the national adaptation programme commits NHS England to build adaptation into new buildings.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A dated official target creates a decade-long procurement runway for cooling, ventilation and building-fabric suppliers.
insights.locator: Government advisers at the Climate Change Committee

insights.claim: Years of underinvestment have left many NHS sites with what the King's Fund calls deteriorating buildings and outdated technology, and many hospitals are old and not designed for increasingly extreme temperatures.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Pre-existing capital backlog means heat adaptation competes with — and compounds — a much larger estate-renewal bill.
insights.locator: As it stands, many NHS hospitals are old

insights.claim: Staff adaptation and reorganisation cannot indefinitely compensate for outdated hospital infrastructure, according to Royal College of Surgeons of England president Tim Lane.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
entities: Royal College of Surgeons of England
insights.so_what: Professional bodies are now publicly pressing for capital spend, a leading indicator of policy movement.
insights.quote: NHS staff work incredibly hard to adapt, often reorganising services and finding practical solutions to keep care running, but resilience alone cannot compensate indefinitely for outdated infrastructure or sustainability.
insights.locator: RCS England president Lane tells Carbon Brief

insights.claim: The UK health secretary has said the NHS has to prepare for summer pressures in the same way it prepares for winter.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Signals a structural shift in NHS planning cycles toward year-round capacity stress, with budget implications.
insights.quote: has to make sure we are preparing for summer pressures now in the same way we prepare for winter
insights.locator: With hospitals once again under significant pressure this summer
